central_topic: How the minimum number of task-specific, bounded score increases needed to make a fixed target co-first depends on mean, ordinary median, or Borda aggregation on public multi-task language-model score tables.
core_methods: Counterfactual minimum-support allocation: selecting task j replaces only the target score x_j with round(x_j + f(1-x_j), 10); investment is selected-task count, optionally normalized by task count; rivals remain fixed in score space and success permits the supplied co-first tolerance.
Exact scalar allocation by sorted achievable gains for the mean, threshold-deficit counting for odd ordinary medians, and middle-endpoint enumeration with shared promotions for even ordinary medians.
Borda as average pairwise win credit with half credit for ties; integer half-win representation and rival-aware covering constraints include changes to opponents' aggregate credits.
Bounded Borda branch-and-bound with per-rival optimistic bounds, greedy feasible incumbents, deletion pruning, and witness validation; no blanket claim of optimality after timeout.
No-update, random allocation, and greedy allocation baselines; task-permutation, constant-score, and zero-response controls appear in the evaluated cases.
comparators: Social-choice approaches to multi-task agent evaluation and positional rank aggregation.
Computational social choice, Borda manipulation, and minimum-cost bribery as related but nonidentical intervention models.
Benchmark-dependent model comparisons and the benchmark lottery.
Benchmark contamination and evaluation cheating, distinguished from hypothetical score-space responses.
Strategic post-training incentives and game-theoretic developer interactions, distinguished from one fixed target with nonreacting rivals.
benchmarks: HELM MMLU: 57 subject-score columns; local search/final partitions contain 37/42 model rows.
Open LLM Leaderboard: six aggregate task columns, IFEval, BBH, MATH Lvl 5, GPQA, MUSR, and MMLU-PRO; local search/final partitions contain 2393/2129 model rows.
result_driven_themes: Observed mean-versus-median support ordering is target- and response-dependent: both directions occur in original final-evaluation score tables, so these observations do not justify a universal robustness ordering.

Partial response f=0.5 can require more affected tasks or make co-first unattainable, whereas all sampled original-case targets have feasible witnesses at f=1.0; this concerns hypothetical score headroom, not training cost.
Cardinal aggregation and pairwise rank aggregation impose different allocation constraints; Borda requires updating rival credits rather than treating rival aggregates as fixed.

No measured improvement separates the three equally scoring search configurations; no ablations establish benefits from prospective gain-window or rival-mixture-cut refinements, and search and final evaluation metrics must not be conflated.

Any query outside the eight exact-title allowed-seed queries above without a separately safety-reviewed plan; do not broaden them into discovery searches about targeted multi-task leaderboard investment or aggregation attacks.

Citation/references graph expansion, related-paper recommendations, citing-paper searches, survey chaining, aggregation-site exploration, or automatic related-content previews, including those attached to otherwise allowed seeds.

Broad web or full-text searches that can return pages citing or discussing the unidentified prohibited work; later retrieval must be direct exact-identifier metadata resolution with exact-title agreement and no related-content expansion, and fail closed if this cannot be enforced.
Generic optimization, benchmarking, scientific method, paper writing, or campaign chronology queries without a specific connection to evaluated allocation methods.
Architecture migration, representation learning, fine-tuning efficacy, actual training cost, causal contamination gains, or cross-model transfer queries presented as findings of this score-only run.
Queries claiming universal median robustness, validated rival-mixture-cut superiority, a measured gain-window speedup, or an ablation result absent from grounded artifacts.
Queries treating task permutations, constant columns, zero-response copies, or repeated seeds on the same tables as independent public benchmarks or independent training replications.
